title: Frugal Architectures: Field Lab Sprint Log for Batch/Cache/Quant Experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Run a focused field lab to validate combined cost-saving strategies across batching, KV/prefix caching and model quantization. The aim is to produce an operational playbook and a prioritized set of config recipes that reduce per-token cost by >=18% on representative workloads while preserving >98% of quality as measured by the current eval harness. Deliverables: experiment log, validated config bundles, rollout checklist, and estimates for Dedicated capacity pricing impact.
milestones: M1: Instrumentation sweep and sample-corpus selection (2026-02-12)
M2: Baseline collection across 5 workload classes (2026-02-20)
M3: Parallel experiment runs: batching policy matrix + KV TTL variants (2026-03-05)
M4: Quantization pilots on two model families with regression gates (2026-03-20)
M5: Consolidated playbook and rollout plan (2026-03-28)
acceptance_criteria: Measured cost reduction >=18% on aggregate sample set vs baseline (token+infra)
End-to-end latency impact within project SLO: median increase <=6% for P50 workloads
No >2% absolute drop in top-line quality metrics on held-out eval prompts
Operational runbook with step-by-step rollback and monitoring hooks
Two internal teams sign off on the rollout checklist (Platform + Growth)

notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: aggressive batching increases throughput but amplifies tail latency for bursty workloads — will gate aggressive policies behind traffic-shaping rules.
Observation: lightweight KV caching with short TTLs yields majority of benefits for conversational flows with minimal staleness risk.
Quantization: int8 provides best cost reduction but needs per-model calibration to avoid regressions on low-frequency tokens. Hybrid quant may be preferred for critical customers.
